note: Engine cases for the BNA smoke-test projection (bna.dmn) — British
Nationality Act 1981 s 1, the de novo (G2) encoding subject.
STATUS 2026-08-02 — 25 cases, GENERATED from the L4 source: one case per
distinct scenario appearing in bna.l4's #ASSERT directives (25 person
scenarios x 9 adoption scenarios, paired person i with adoption i mod 9 so
every #ASSERT scenario of both kinds is exercised at least twice for
adoptions, once for persons). The model has THREE inputData — `person`,
`adoption`, `entitled_under_subsection_3_3A_or_4` — because the exporter's
D-PARAM-AS-INPUT lowering un-lifts each GIVEN parameter to one GLOBAL
input; a case therefore carries one person AND one adoption world, and
the s 41A grant-gate flag is set true exactly on the five subsection (4)
cases so `registration_may_be_granted` reproduces the two #ASSERTs on the
grant gate (lead case: granted; applicant of bad character: not granted).
ACTIVATION CONTRACT (house rule, per regcf-corpus.cases.json): every
value in `expect` is derived from the L4 SOURCE — evaluated with the
prebuilt l4 binary over a copy of bna.l4 carrying one #EVAL per (case,
decision), 979 evaluations in all, cross-checked against the file's own
42 #ASSERT directives (all satisfied on the same run) — NEVER from a DMN
engine's own output. A pin regenerated from the thing it pins is vacuous.
KNOWN BLOCKING DEFECT CARRIED HONESTLY: bna.fidelity.txt records 3
blocking D-LITERALEXPR — the dated constants `commencement`,
`the_appointed_day`, `the_relevant_day` are emitted as raw L4 text
(`YMD OF 1983, 1, 1`) with no FEEL rendering. Their pins below are the L4
truth ($date 1983-01-01 / 2002-05-21 / 2010-01-13); whatever an engine
does with the raw-L4 bodies is a MEASUREMENT, not a target — do not
adjust these pins to make an engine pass, and do not delete cases.
MEASURED 2026-08-02 on both engines at the R12/R13 tree plus this file:
BOTH REFUSE WHOLE-FILE on exactly those three expressions, so not one of
the 25 x 43 pins below was ever compared. Banners verbatim:
* KIE 8.44.0.Final: XSD valid; VALID 3 error(s) + BUILD 3 error(s),
all ERR_COMPILING_FEEL 'syntax error near ''OF''' on
decision_commencement_literal / decision_the_appointed_day_literal /
decision_the_relevant_day_literal; BUILD errors abort before any
case runs. 'KIE 8.44.0.Final VERDICT: 1 file(s), 0 case(s),
6 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0/0 decision(s) SUCCEEDED, 0/0 value(s)
as expected, 0/0 service output value(s) as expected   <<< FAILED',
exit 1.
* Camunda 8.7.6 (zeebe-dmn): 'PARSE  INVALID: FEEL expression: failed
to parse expression ''YMD OF 1983, 1, 1'': Expected
(binaryComparison | between | instanceOf | in | "and" | "or" |
end-of-input):1:5, found "OF 1983, 1"' (and the same for the 2002
and 2010 constants). 'Camunda 8.7.6 (zeebe-dmn) VERDICT: 1 file(s),
0 case(s), 0 parsed, 1 error(s), 0/0 decision(s) evaluated,
0/0 value(s) as expected   <<< FAILED', exit 1.
This is the regcf pre-R12 refusal shape reproduced on a fresh corpus:
a standalone dated constant (GIVETH A DATE ... MEANS YMD y m d) has no
FEEL lowering, where regcf's dated constants survived only because the
rule-version axis turned them into guarded chains. The fix belongs in
the exporter (YMD y m d -> FEEL date(y,m,d)), not in these pins.
CAUSE ISOLATED + PINS PROVEN, same day: a SCRATCH copy of bna.dmn with
ONLY those three <text> lines rewritten to FEEL date literals
nothing else changed goes fully green on BOTH engines against THIS file:

1075/1075 decision(s) SUCCEEDED, 1075/1075 value(s) as expected,
325/325 service output value(s) as expected', exit 0.
* Camunda 8.7.6 (zeebe-dmn): '1 file(s), 25 case(s), 1 parsed,
0 error(s), 1075/1075 decision(s) evaluated, 1075/1075 value(s) as
expected', exit 0.
So the missing YMD lowering is the SOLE defect between bna.dmn and a
